messages:
mira: quick flag: Triton9b-grouped hybrid quant onboarding failing evals on long-answer QA. answers swapping subject/verb in ~9% of cases.
tomas: swapped how? examples?
mira: short repro: question about ‘The committee and the mayor’ -> model attributes actions to wrong agent. FP16 baseline fine. grouped-head quant (groups of 8 heads -> 8 groups) shows flips.
ryan: which quant pipeline? grouping for kernel packing?
mira: quant-pack v2 with head-grouping (pack-size=8), LP16->int4 core + per-group int3 bias. exporter also runs vocab-merge step (we recently added soft-hyphen handle).
alisa: soft-hyphen? did vocab indices change between exports? that could offset embedding matrix rows and misalign KV caches.
mira: I diffed vocab hashes: exporter added soft-hyphen token at index 5021, bumped later ids. but model binary uses permuted head storage for grouped layout: head_index_map serialized as [0,8,16,...] ordering. runtime expects canonical contiguous ordering.
tomas: so two independent transforms: vocab-shift + head-group packing -> addresses now point to different semantic embeddings and different rotary head scales. ugly.
ryan: any numeric evidence?
mira: yes: diffs from interpret dump:
- fp16: embed[5025] ~ 0.0043 0.0021 -0.0039
- grouped-hybrid: embed[5025] ~ -0.112 0.210 0.019 (looks like different row)
and head phase mismatch on head_group_3: `mean_cos_diff = 0.97` vs `0.01`
alisa: that level of phase delta will absolutely flip sign on some attention basis vectors -> meaning slot assignment changes.
qa-bot: regression-detected: longqa-suite answer-entity-consistency dropped 8.9% on triton9b-grouped at 2025-02-02T10:12:01Z
buildbot: exporter run log: `vocab_merge: added_token=\u00AD at idx=5021; head_pack: groups=8, stride=64; head_map_serialized=true`
tomas: mitigation options: 1) revert vocab merge for the nightly hybrid builds; 2) change exporter to emit explicit head_map and canonical_vocab_map and have runtime validate on load; 3) broadcast rotary_scale per-group to runtime and run a short calibration.
ryan: we should do both 2 and 3. short-term revert vocab change to stop customer impact. long-term add strict checks.
mira: wrote a quick shim that reorders head tensor back to canonical order on load and remaps embedding rows by comparing md5(vocab) in model file vs canonical vocab md5. patched local runtime -> reduced swap-rate to 0.6% on the news-100 sweep.
alisa: nice. please prod a PR for the runtime loader checks and put a failing unit test that simulates a vocab index shift + grouped head permutation.
mira: PR: https://github.com/redwood/inference-runtime/pull/218 (draft) 

reproducer snippet for QA:
```
# reproducer: detect misaligned export
from redwood import ModelLoader
m = ModelLoader('/tmp/triton9b-grouped')
print('vocab_md5', m.metadata.vocab_md5)
print('head_map', m.metadata.head_map[:16])
# run small eval
from redwood.eval import run_longqa
print(run_longqa(m, dataset='longqa-sample', max_examples=50))
```

ryan: also add a conversion-time checksum: exporter should write `vocab_md5` and `head_map_crc32` to metadata. conversion must fail if head_map doesn't match expected dims.
tomas: long-term we should avoid mutable in-place vocab merges unless we emit a mapping table (old_idx->new_idx). that'll make remapping deterministic.\alysa: (typo) alisa: yup. I'll add that note to the RFC.
qa-bot: note: if you revert vocab merge, restart nightly quant job to pick up corrected files.
buildbot: rolling back triton9b-grouped hybrid artifacts in 5m unless new build lands.
mira: I'm kicking a fix now: adding loader checksum + auto-remap fallback. will ping when PR is up. thanks :sparkles:
